title: Smell Detectives: Parent Guide
endLine: Much of flavor comes from aromas that reach your nose.

scenes.tts: Why does food taste so dull when you have a cold? A few covered cups and a pinched nose let your child find out for themselves.
scenes.caption: Why does food taste so dull when you have a cold? A few covered cups and a pinched nose let your child find out for themselves.
scenes.visual: Friendly schematic kitchen table. A bowl of soup sits in front of a simple drawn face with a tissue and a stuffy-nose cloud; the steam lines above the bowl look faint and gray. Large text: 'Why does food taste dull with a cold?' No photos of real children.
scenes.narration: Why does food taste so dull when you have a cold? A few covered cups and a pinched nose let your child find out for themselves.

scenes.visual: Same table. Title 'Smell Detectives' appears for 2 seconds; the soup steam curls slowly.

scenes.tts: This takes about thirty minutes, with kitchen foods. Your child practices describing smells in words, matching by smell alone, and checking a prediction. They find out how much of flavor comes from the nose.
scenes.caption: This takes about thirty minutes, with kitchen foods. Your child practices describing smells in words, matching by smell alone, and checking a prediction. They find out how much of flavor comes from the nose.
scenes.visual: The soup slides aside; a row of plain paper cups appears on the table. Three labels appear one by one: 'Describe in words', 'Match by smell', 'Predict and check'.
scenes.narration: This takes about thirty minutes, with kitchen foods. Your child practices describing smells in words, matching by smell alone, and checking a prediction. They find out how much of flavor comes from the nose.

scenes.tts: Stay with your child throughout. Use kitchen foods only. Skip essential oils, perfume, cleaners, and unknown liquids. Check food allergies before choosing ingredients. Skip nuts and nut products. Use latex-free bands if anyone has a latex allergy.
scenes.caption: Stay with your child throughout. Use kitchen foods only. Skip essential oils, perfume, cleaners, and unknown liquids. Check food allergies before choosing ingredients. Skip nuts and nut products. Use latex-free bands if anyone has a latex allergy.
scenes.visual: Keep the kitchen table in view. Show an adult beside the child, choosing foods. Cross out an essential oil bottle and a bag of nuts. Show the adult checking the rubber-band package.
scenes.narration: Stay with your child throughout. Use kitchen foods only. Skip essential oils, perfume, cleaners, and unknown liquids. Check food allergies before choosing ingredients. Skip nuts and nut products. Use latex-free bands if anyone has a latex allergy.

scenes.tts: Put a cotton ball in each paper cup you cannot see through. Add one kitchen smell to each pair. Try orange peel, coffee, a cinnamon stick, vanilla, or a crushed mint leaf.
scenes.caption: Put a cotton ball in each paper cup you cannot see through. Add one kitchen smell to each pair. Try orange peel, coffee, a cinnamon stick, vanilla, or a crushed mint leaf.
scenes.visual: Cotton balls drop into the cups. Above each pair of cups, a kitchen item appears and a small piece moves into both cups: a strip of orange peel, a pinch of ground coffee, a cinnamon stick piece, drops of vanilla, a crushed mint leaf.
scenes.narration: Put a cotton ball in each paper cup you cannot see through. Add one kitchen smell to each pair. Try orange peel, coffee, a cinnamon stick, vanilla, or a crushed mint leaf.

scenes.tts: You cover each cup with foil and a rubber band. Poke four or five holes with a pencil, with the cup on the table. Label the cups with letters and keep a secret key.
scenes.caption: You cover each cup with foil and a rubber band. Poke four or five holes with a pencil, with the cup on the table. Label the cups with letters and keep a secret key.
scenes.visual: An adult's hands smooth foil over each cup and snap on a band, then poke holes with a pencil while the cup sits on the table. Letters A, B, C, D appear on the cups; a small folded 'secret key' card slides under a book.
scenes.narration: You cover each cup with foil and a rubber band. Poke four or five holes with a pencil, with the cup on the table. Label the cups with letters and keep a secret key.

scenes.tts: Show your child how to waft. Hold a cup a hand’s width below the nose. Wave the air toward your face and sniff gently. Ask, 'Is it strong or faint? Pleasant or not?' Mix up the cups and find the pairs.
scenes.caption: Show your child how to waft. Hold a cup a hand’s width below the nose. Wave the air toward your face and sniff gently. Ask, 'Is it strong or faint? Pleasant or not?' Mix up the cups and find the pairs.
scenes.visual: A schematic hand waves gently above a cup, with soft curved smell lines drifting toward a simple drawn nose. Speech bubble: 'Strong or faint?' Two matching cups slide together side by side, then two more.
scenes.narration: Show your child how to waft. Hold a cup a hand’s width below the nose. Wave the air toward your face and sniff gently. Ask, 'Is it strong or faint? Pleasant or not?' Mix up the cups and find the pairs.

scenes.tts: Next, guess what each smell is, then peel back the foil to check. It is common to know a smell well and still not find its name. Ask, 'Where have you smelled this before?'
scenes.caption: Next, guess what each smell is, then peel back the foil to check. It is common to know a smell well and still not find its name. Ask, 'Where have you smelled this before?'
scenes.visual: Guesses appear on small sticky notes beside each pair: 'Candy?', 'Christmas?'. The foil peels back on one cup to show a mint leaf; a check mark appears. A speech bubble: 'Where have you smelled this before?'
scenes.narration: Next, guess what each smell is, then peel back the foil to check. It is common to know a smell well and still not find its name. Ask, 'Where have you smelled this before?'

scenes.tts: Make two covered vanilla cups. Add one drop to one cotton ball and six to the other. You handle the extract because it contains alcohol. Close it and put it out of reach. Compare the smells, resting a minute between rounds.
scenes.caption: Make two covered vanilla cups. Add one drop to one cotton ball and six to the other. You handle the extract because it contains alcohol. Close it and put it out of reach. Compare the smells, resting a minute between rounds.
scenes.visual: Keep the kitchen table. The adult adds one drop to the first cup and six to the second, covers both, then closes the bottle and puts it out of reach. Show two gentle wafts with a waiting clock between rounds.
scenes.narration: Make two covered vanilla cups. Add one drop to one cotton ball and six to the other. You handle the extract because it contains alcohol. Close it and put it out of reach. Compare the smells, resting a minute between rounds.

scenes.tts: Use the smell cups only for smelling. Wash hands after handling the ingredients. Skip tasting if your child has trouble swallowing. Have them sit, take small sips, and swallow before talking.
scenes.caption: Use the smell cups only for smelling. Wash hands after handling the ingredients. Skip tasting if your child has trouble swallowing. Have them sit, take small sips, and swallow before talking.
scenes.visual: Keep the smell cups on the table with a crossed-out mouth icon. Show hands being washed, then return to the table and show the child seated beside the adult.
scenes.narration: Use the smell cups only for smelling. Wash hands after handling the ingredients. Skip tasting if your child has trouble swallowing. Have them sit, take small sips, and swallow before talking.

scenes.tts: Pour two juices that look alike, such as apple and white grape, into separate small cups. Mark them one and two. Then have your child close their eyes and pinch their nose.
scenes.caption: Pour two juices that look alike, such as apple and white grape, into separate small cups. Mark them one and two. Then have your child close their eyes and pinch their nose.
scenes.visual: Two small cups of pale juice, labelled 1 and 2, sit side by side and look identical. A simple drawn child-figure (schematic, no real child) sits at the table with eyes closed and fingers gently pinching the nose.
scenes.narration: Pour two juices that look alike, such as apple and white grape, into separate small cups. Mark them one and two. Then have your child close their eyes and pinch their nose.

scenes.tts: Before your child sips, make a prediction. With their nose pinched, will they be able to tell which juice it is?
scenes.caption: Before your child sips, make a prediction. With their nose pinched, will they be able to tell which juice it is?
scenes.visual: Hold on the two identical juice cups. Show the question 'Can they tell which juice?' Keep the cups untouched while the parent thinks.
scenes.narration: Before your child sips, make a prediction. With their nose pinched, will they be able to tell which juice it is?

scenes.visual: Hold the same question and both untouched cups. Give the juice a subtle ripple. Keep the answer hidden.

scenes.tts: Offer a small sip. Have your child signal their guess with their fingers. Then they let go of their nose and swallow. Ask, 'What changed when you let go?' Offer water, then repeat with the other juice.
scenes.caption: Offer a small sip. Have your child signal their guess with their fingers. Then they let go of their nose and swallow. Ask, 'What changed when you let go?' Offer water, then repeat with the other juice.
scenes.visual: At the same table, the seated child takes a small sip, answers with fingers, releases their nose, then swallows. An arrow traces aroma from the mouth to the nose. The adult offers water, then the other juice.
scenes.narration: Offer a small sip. Have your child signal their guess with their fingers. Then they let go of their nose and swallow. Ask, 'What changed when you let go?' Offer water, then repeat with the other juice.

scenes.tts: As you breathe out after a sip, aromas can travel from the back of your mouth to your nose. Your brain combines smell and taste. Pinching your nose makes much of the flavor fade.
scenes.caption: As you breathe out after a sip, aromas can travel from the back of your mouth to your nose. Your brain combines smell and taste. Pinching your nose makes much of the flavor fade.
scenes.visual: Show a side-view head outline. Trace a curved path from the mouth into the nose, then dim it as fingers pinch the nostrils. Label the path 'Food aromas' and leave the taste signal visible.
scenes.narration: As you breathe out after a sip, aromas can travel from the back of your mouth to your nose. Your brain combines smell and taste. Pinching your nose makes much of the flavor fade.

scenes.tts: Keep cotton balls, rubber bands, and other small pieces away from children under four. Call nine one one if a child is choking and cannot cough, cry, or talk.
scenes.caption: Keep cotton balls, rubber bands, and other small pieces away from children under four. Call nine one one if a child is choking and cannot cough, cry, or talk.
scenes.visual: The adult clears the table and puts small items out of reach. Show two short cards in sequence: 'Choking risk under four' and 'Call 911 for choking'.
scenes.narration: Keep cotton balls, rubber bands, and other small pieces away from children under four. Call nine one one if a child is choking and cannot cough, cry, or talk.

scenes.tts: Why does food taste dull with a cold? A stuffy nose makes it harder to smell the food. Compare what your child noticed with what you predicted.
scenes.caption: Why does food taste dull with a cold? A stuffy nose makes it harder to smell the food. Compare what your child noticed with what you predicted.
scenes.visual: Return to the opening soup bowl. Show faint aroma lines at the stuffy nose. Bring back the two juice cups beside the bowl as the parent and child compare their observations.
scenes.narration: Why does food taste dull with a cold? A stuffy nose makes it harder to smell the food. Compare what your child noticed with what you predicted.

scenes.visual: End card over the brightened soup and the row of cups. Large centered text: 'Much of flavor comes from aromas that reach your nose.'
scenes.line: Much of flavor comes from aromas that reach your nose.
